text:
jess: FYI customer ACME hitting lots of 504s on hosted API, started ~12:10Z. stack shows scale events but requests time out.
jess: gateway logs:
```
[2026-03-10T12:11:22Z] upstream_read_timeout route=/v1/generate tenant=acme-corp queue_depth=118
[2026-03-10T12:12:05Z] 504 gateway_timeout tenant=acme-corp request_id=...
```

tom: which infra path? hosted/redwood-api or dedicated pool?
jess: hosted inference (prod-us-east), route /v1/generate. customer says spike after campaign.
rick: putting oncall eyes. @maya can you check KEDA/HPA events for that tenant quickly?
maya: looking. `kubectl get events -n inference | grep acme` shows repeated scale up requests from KEDA around 12:11-12:13 but pods stayed in ContainerCreating for ~90s. see event: `FailedMount` then `SuccessfullyMounted` later.

jess: stack dump from proxy:
```
proxy: upstream request queued -> timed out after 30s waiting for backend
keda-controller: triggered scale to 8 (minReplicaCount=1 -> desired=8)
hpa: scaled to 3 (metrics lagging)
```

rick: hmm HPA and KEDA targets disagree, and kube is creating pods but readiness delay looks long.
maya: checking scaledobject config for acme, found cooldownPeriod=300 and pollingInterval=60 and minReplicaCount=1. also annotations include `scaledobject.keda.sh/activationThreshold: "5"` which may be wrong for burst traffic.

maya: config snippet:
```
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: acme-scaledobject
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    name: acme-runtime
  pollingInterval: 60
  cooldownPeriod: 300
  minReplicaCount: 1
  triggers:
  - type: redis
    metadata:
      listName: inference-queue
      listLength: "10"
```

tom: that pollingInterval is large for sudden bursts -> KEDA will react slowly. cooldown too long too.
jess: customer SLA complaining, opened support ticket (ACME-4567), escalating.
sarah-cs: I'm on the call with them at 12:30PT.
rick: also seeing image pull slow on two pods; node had EBS attach delay (PersistentVolume claim binding) for model cache. pods stuck while PV attach completed -> long warmup.
maya: readinessProbe has initialDelaySeconds=60 and timeoutSeconds=1, but model init takes ~40-70s depending on quantized weights. combined with PV attach this adds 60-90s to readiness.

jess: repro steps in staging suggested by customer:
1) flood /v1/generate simultaneously from 100 clients for 30s
2) watch redis queue length >50
3) observe KEDA scale event and HPA mismatch

rick: quick mitigation: bump minReplicaCount to 3 for acme, reduce pollingInterval to 10, cooldownPeriod to 90, add prewarm annotation to ensure model caches warm on start. Also set podDisruptionBudget and nodeSelector for nodes with cached volumes.
maya: patch I suggest (kubectl apply):
```
spec:
  minReplicaCount: 3
  pollingInterval: 10
  cooldownPeriod: 90
  triggers:
    - metadata:
        listLength: "8"
```

tom: can we add temporary weighted routing to divert 30% of ACME traffic to dedicated reserved pool while we stabilize?
jess: ops: yes, we have burst capacity but need to flip routing flag. @deploy-bot can you create a canary route change for acme now?
deploy-bot: canary route change created: route=acme -> 30% dedicated-pool at 1768877890. Monitoring hooks added.

rick: after canary flip we saw 50% drop in 504s within 120s. still some tails at 12:22.
maya: still logging a few ContainerCreating events due to PV attach; engineering to look at model cache preloading to avoid PV mount latency.

jess: immediate actions captured:
- set minReplicaCount=3 for acme (done at 12:16Z)
- reduce KEDA pollingInterval to 10, cooldownPeriod 90 (done 12:17Z)
- enable 30% dedicated routing canary (deployed 12:18Z)
- opened ENG ticket: ENG-2987 to add prewarm lifecycle hook + avoid synchronous PV attach during scale-up

sarah-cs: CS informed customer, offered temporary rate-limiting and status updates.
rick: next steps: schedule a short playbook to prewarm model cache for large tenants, add automations to reconcile HPA desired vs KEDA desired within 5s, and investigate pod scheduling blockers (PV/pvc speed).

tom: tagging this P1 until ENG-2987 and a postmortem done. closing live incident channel after 2h post stabilization.
jess: thanks all :thumbsup:
